findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, committed to source control and visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. Credentials should come from IAM execution roles or Secrets Manager/SSM Parameter Store.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so Lambda environment variables (which here hold secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are decrypted and displayed in the console to any principal with read access to the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy should be used.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that reached end of support and no longer receives security patches for the runtime or underlying OS packages.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
